palette.mood: Lamplit deep-sea study. Bering teal-black water and a dark bench, one warm brass lamp, a pearl otolith that is the brightest object in every frame, and a single near-infrared magenta that means ONLY the machine's light and its signature.
palette.divergence: September 30th was fog slate, peat and a warning orange on a phone and a binder. September 23rd was Air Force paper and statements. This film has no document pile at all, it lives in water, under a microscope lamp and in a timber hangar, and its accent is NIR magenta, used on nothing human.
palette.brass_rule: Brass #C8963E only on small hard-edged parts (rails, objective, plates, counter, trophy), never a background wash, so teal-black stays the dominant field. The engineers' trophy is brass, never magenta.

light.time: Night at the bench, a single warm lamp
light.direction: Key from the microscope lamp upper left (warm #FFD58A), cool teal fill from the water and archive dark, magenta rim ONLY on the spectrometer beam and spectral line
light.depth: Three planes per set: dark archive or water behind, the bench or stone in the middle, the reader's hands and the counter foreground. GradeLayer warm bloom on the lamp, NightGrade style vignette. lib/lighting tones() ramps on brass.

per_set.aleutian-water: cool caustic key from above, teal fill, a pearl rim on the otolith so the stone is the brightest object when it pops
per_set.bench: warm lamp key upper left, teal fill, magenta rim only on the beam
per_set.machine-interior: magenta beam as the only key, the slot rimmed in brass, the question mark lit pearl
per_set.archive and hangar: one hanging lamp pool at centre, cool falloff to the far drawers, drawer pulls catch glints
per_set.staircase: the reader's lamp across the hall keys the stairs warm from the left, teal fill, the manager's pen catches the lamp

shape_language.grammar: Concentric rings (organic, counted, human) against straight lines and rails (the machine, the spectrum, the staircase). The otolith is an irregular rounded bean with rings; the spectrometer is rectilinear brass on straight rails; the spectral line is a jagged straight-segment polyline.
shape_language.why: The turn is the straight line resolving back into ring ticks, so the contrast has to be legible from frame 1.
shape_language.turn: At the turn the straight magenta spectral line tears into tally ticks, and the ticks CURVE as they fall and settle as concentric arcs around an otolith core, so the line literally becomes rings. Each tick shifts colour from accent #E0336B to hero pearl #EDE3CC as it lands, and the outermost ring lands in lamp #FFD58A on the final click. After that the only magenta left in the button is the rim of the NIRReader plate.

motion_language.world: Water drifts with suspended particles, the lamp breathes, archive drawers parallax. Rings pulse core outward on every click, the tally digits roll with overshoot.
hero_moves: the otolith pop out of the rockfish with anticipation, 180 degree motion blur and spin settle
the NIR spectrometer sliding in on rails with overshoot and a brass clank
the machine tag bouncing off the sealed NEXT STEP slot with squash and an ImpactStar
the spectral line peeling off and resolving into tally ticks

composition.focal: The shot's named hero is always the brightest, best-finished object at the frame centre. The magenta beam never outshines the pearl stone.
composition.negative_space: the archive dark and the water carry the negative space, the lamp pool frames the subject
composition.safe_area: hero action and plates inside y 420 to 1500 for the square, atmosphere above and bench foreground below
composition.signature_shot: Inside the 1930s timber hangar: a propeller on a beam where planes should be, drawers glinting to a vanishing point like a starfield (held 0.7s), an archivist in a lamp pool carrying a tray of drawers, and an archive otolith pair tagged 1960s rising from one drawer under the brass Chamberlin plate. The 1878 stone is NOT in the hangar (it was collected in 2022).

craft_advance: none needed beyond the net-new otolith family
